how: Changi Sailing Club runs public beginner sailing courses.
SAF Yacht Club runs adult Level 1 sailing and kids intro dinghy programmes.
One15 Marina Club in Sentosa Cove offers sailing courses to members and non-members.
Rent single kayaks by the 2-hour block on the Kallang Basin; no licence needed.
venue: Singapore Sports Hub Water Sports Centre

how: Guided kayak tours through Pulau Ubin mangroves, reached by bumboat from Changi Point.
SUP lessons and board hire at Sentosa's Tanjong Beach.
SUP Yoga Singapore runs lessons at Mana Mana Beach Club.
venue: Mana Mana Beach Club (SUP Yoga Singapore)

how: Constant Wind at NSRCC Changi runs windsurfing courses; East Coast Park also has schools.
Lessons are advertised at East Coast Park, but light and unreliable wind limits sessions.
venue: Mana Mana Beach Club (Windsurfing, Kitesurfing & SUP school)

how: PADI courses and fun dives at Pulau Hantu; visibility is often only 2-3 m.
Freedive SG / Singapore Freediving Academy runs multi-agency freediving courses.
Snorkel off Lazarus, Kusu and Hantu islands; visibility is usually under 5 m.
Cable-park wakeboarding with instructors on a beginner cable system.
Singapore Wake Park is the country's cable-ski park, with three cable systems.
Done on the cable systems at Singapore Wake Park rather than behind a boat.
Wind-tunnel flights at Sentosa (formerly iFLY Singapore, now Altitude X); not a real jump.
No drop zone or airspace for civilian jumps in Singapore; nearest are in Malaysia and Thailand.
No cliffs or permitted structures, and jumping is illegal in Singapore.
Singapore's sheltered straits have no rideable surf; people travel to Malaysia, Indonesia or Bali.
Wave House Sentosa, the FlowRider venue, closed in October 2019 and I found no reopening.
Beginner dragon boat sessions at Kallang by AustCham Paddle Club and other teams.
venue: AustCham Paddle Club (Kallang Dragon Boat Nursery)

how: AustCham Paddle Club also runs outrigger canoe paddling out of Marina Bay.
PAssion WaVe at Marina Bay hires pedal boats, bell boats and kayaks.
Singapore Rowing Association runs a Learn-to-Row course: ergometer basics then quad boat on water.
Free shore fishing at designated grounds such as Kranji Reservoir Park; no licence for angling.
Pay-per-session saltwater fishing pond at Pasir Ris Town Park.
Open fields designated for uncrewed aircraft, e.g. Pandan Reservoir; drones over 250g must be registered.
Restricted airspace and goggle rules limit it to approved fields or indoor sub-250g whoops.
venue: Multi-Rotor Association of Singapore sanctioned fields

how: Flying fields exist but are scarce; I could not confirm a public club field.
Mostly via school Singapore Youth Flying Club CCAs; no clear public club found.
No balloon operators; dense airspace around Changi, Paya Lebar and Seletar bars it.
No hills or launch sites and no permitted flying zones; nearest sites are in Malaysia.
No suitable terrain or airspace; people go to Malaysia or Thailand.
No public gliding club in Singapore; the RSAF-linked youth programme is school-based.
No rapids; the nearest are in Malaysia or Nepal.
No flooded caves; the nearest are in Malaysia, Thailand or Mexico.
Open lawns such as Marina Barrage are popular for flying kites.
